Our proof closely follows the proof of the following result of Rónyai, Babai, and Ganapathy, which provides a bound on the number of zero-patterns of general sequences of polynomials:

Theorem 3.4. ([[5], Theorem 4.1])Let $$f_1,\ldots ,f_T$$ be a sequence of polynomials in $$N$$ variables, where each polynomial has degree at most $$d$$. For any $$t$$, the number of zero-patterns is at most

$$$$\begin{equation*} {\left(\binom{T}{0}+\cdots +\binom{T}{t} \right)}+\binom{N+(T-t-1)d}{N}. \end{equation*}$$$$

Our proof uses the key ideas from the proof of Theorem 3.4, with the main difference being that we can estimate the degrees of polynomials more carefully in the specific case of the sequence $$\lbrace  P^{(j)}(\lambda _i) \rbrace$$.

Theorem 3.6.

For any nonsimple local topological type \(\mathbf{T}\) and any order of precision \(N\), the \(N\)th-order approximation of the volume function \(V_g^{\mathbf{T}}\) is a Friedman–Ramanujan function in the weak sense.

The full result contains more information on the uniformity of the degrees, constants, and coefficients of the Friedman–Ramanujan functions, which is required to obtain a spectral gap. The weak sense refers to a weaker, integrated, definition of Friedman–Ramanujan functions.

The last significant challenge tackled in the proof of Theorem 3.4 comes from the necessity to remove tangles, as mentioned above in Lipnowski and Wright’s approach. There it is solved following the lines of Friedman’s work. The basic idea is to rewrite the indicator function of the set of tangle-free surfaces as a sum of geometric functions, similarly to (3.5). However, past the precision \(\frac {3}{16}\), one needs to include tangles (surfaces of Euler characteristic -1 with a short boundary) in this inclusion-exclusion. Contrarily to short closed geodesic, these tangles can intersect, and one hence a priori needs to list all possible combinations of tangles. This issue is solved by proving a Moebius formula in [7], which achieves exactly the goal stated above, while avoiding tedious topological enumerations.
